collection: NECO BECE Islamic Studies JSS 3 original ethics practice
note: Original written objective practice with provisional historical topic mapping. Current adoption, full scope, official option counts and paper allocation remain unverified. No Arabic recitation or tajwid performance is assessed.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply impartial justice and explain the consequences of unfair treatment.
questions.prompt: A pupil sees a close relative damage a shared classroom cupboard. When asked what happened, which response best applies the justice principle in Qur’an 4:135?
options: Blame a less popular pupil to protect the relative.
Give an honest account even though the relative may be criticised.
Describe the damage only if the relative gives permission.
Change the account according to the relative's wealth.
questions.answer: Give an honest account even though the relative may be criticised.
questions.explanation: The verse calls for impartial testimony even when oneself or close relatives are involved.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply impartial justice and explain the consequences of unfair treatment.
questions.prompt: Two teams have quarrelled before a match. The referee dislikes one team. Which decision best reflects the principle checked in Qur’an 5:8?
options: Give the disliked team a disadvantage to prevent complaints from friends.
Ignore all rule-breaking by the disliked team to appear generous.
Let the team captains decide which fouls should count after the match.
Apply the agreed rules consistently despite personal dislike.
questions.answer: Apply the agreed rules consistently despite personal dislike.
questions.explanation: Hostility should not lead to unjust treatment. Consistent rules avoid favouring either side.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply impartial justice and explain the consequences of unfair treatment.
questions.prompt: A school has limited copies of a large-print reading sheet. The teacher gives those copies to pupils who need them to read the lesson. Why can this arrangement be equitable?
options: It responds to a relevant need so pupils can access the same learning.
It proves that some pupils deserve more respect than others.
It means all materials must always be distributed by friendship.
It removes the need to explain allocation decisions.
questions.answer: It responds to a relevant need so pupils can access the same learning.
questions.explanation: Equity can require support suited to a relevant need, rather than identical materials regardless of access.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Apply impartial justice and explain the consequences of unfair treatment.
questions.prompt: A club repeatedly gives prizes to the organiser's friends despite published judging criteria. Which consequence is most directly connected to this unfairness?
options: Participants will always improve their work.
Published criteria will become easier to understand.
Members may lose trust in the competition and stop taking part.
Every participant will receive equal recognition.
questions.answer: Members may lose trust in the competition and stop taking part.
questions.explanation: Disregarding criteria in favour of friends undermines confidence in the process and discourages participation.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Identify conduct that demonstrates consideration for neighbours.
questions.prompt: A family is new to a compound and has no relatives there. Which judgement best fits the neighbourly kindness taught in Qur’an 4:36?
options: Kindness applies only after the family becomes related by marriage.
The family may be treated considerately even without a kinship connection.
The family must first provide gifts to every household.
Neighbours have no reason to recognise one another's needs.
questions.answer: The family may be treated considerately even without a kinship connection.
questions.explanation: The verse includes kindness to neighbours beyond close relatives. Kinship is not a condition for consideration.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Identify conduct that demonstrates consideration for neighbours.
questions.prompt: A household plans a noisy repair that may disturb nearby residents. Which action best demonstrates good neighbourliness?
options: Start at any hour because the work is inside their home.
Ask neighbours to leave the compound for the whole week.
Post pictures of complaining neighbours to discourage objections.
Discuss the likely disturbance in advance and agree reasonable working times.
questions.answer: Discuss the likely disturbance in advance and agree reasonable working times.
questions.explanation: Advance communication and reasonable timing consider neighbours' needs while allowing the repair to proceed.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Identify conduct that demonstrates consideration for neighbours.
questions.prompt: A learner hears an unverified rumour that a neighbour has cheated customers. Which response best protects good neighbourly relations while respecting the need for truth?
options: Avoid circulating the claim as fact and seek reliable clarification if a concern needs to be raised.
Post the rumour widely so the neighbour must defend it.
Add details that make the story more convincing.
Assume the rumour is true because several friends repeat it.
questions.answer: Avoid circulating the claim as fact and seek reliable clarification if a concern needs to be raised.
questions.explanation: Repeating an unsupported accusation can damage a neighbour's reputation. Responsible clarification distinguishes a concern from an established fact.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish unethical conduct and explain its effects on shared trust.
questions.prompt: A person offers a committee member a private payment on condition that their application is moved ahead of others. Which feature makes this ethically different from an openly recorded donation with no promised favour?
options: The amount of money is written in naira.
Both payments involve a committee.
The private payment seeks preferential treatment in return.
The applicant knows the committee member's name.
questions.answer: The private payment seeks preferential treatment in return.
questions.explanation: The promised private benefit is tied to an improper favour, which is the key ethical issue.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish unethical conduct and explain its effects on shared trust.
questions.prompt: A storekeeper takes donated school supplies home without permission and removes them from the stock record. Which description most directly fits the conduct?
options: Neighbourly assistance because the goods were donated.
Taking shared property dishonestly and concealing it.
Fair distribution because the storekeeper handled the goods first.
An approved reward because no price was charged.
questions.answer: Taking shared property dishonestly and concealing it.
questions.explanation: Donation does not transfer ownership to the storekeeper. Unauthorised taking and concealment breach trust.

questions.subject: Islamic Studies
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish unethical conduct and explain its effects on shared trust.
questions.prompt: A committee selects suppliers after receiving secret personal benefits. Even when the purchased goods arrive, why does the conduct remain harmful?
options: Delivery automatically makes any selection process fair.
Private benefits guarantee that the best supplier was chosen.
Only missing goods can ever damage public confidence.
Decisions may serve private interests and weaken trust in the use of shared resources.
questions.answer: Decisions may serve private interests and weaken trust in the use of shared resources.
questions.explanation: The conflict of interest can distort selection and undermine trust even if some goods are delivered.
